newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK democrats on lobbying mission to Australia, NZ.
newsitem.headline: HK democrats on lobbying mission to Australia, NZ.

text.p: The leader of Hong Kong's biggest pro-democracy party said on Monday he would meet top officials in Australia and New Zealand to lobby for visa-free entry for Hong Kong people after it returns to China in 1997.

Democratic Party chairman Martin Lee will lead a delegation to Australia and New Zealand from Tuesday to December 8. Lee said they would meet the countries' foreign ministers, deputy prime ministers and other parliamentarians.

They would urge Australia's immigration minister to grant visa-free access to holders of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) passports, which will be issued after the British colony is handed over to China at midnight on June 30 next year.
Besides Britain, only Singapore and Western Samoa have promised SAR passport holders visa-free entry.
The capitalist city will revert to communist rule but has been promised a high degree of autonomy after the handover.
Lee said he would also explain the future of the rule of law and human rights in Hong Kong as well as the possible dangers it faced.
China plans to replace the territory's elected legislature with a provisional body until further China-sponsored elections in 1998.
